IBM.rationale: IBM presents a moderately attractive fundamental picture. The company is executing a successful strategic pivot toward higher-margin software (11% YoY growth in Q1 2026, now 45% of revenue) with strong AI momentum ($12.5B cumulative GenAI bookings). The z17 mainframe super-cycle is driving a 51% hardware revenue surge, and operating margins expanded 140bps YoY to 14%. However, the stock has already re-rated significantly from its 2025 lows (PE compressed from ~50x to ~26x as earnings caught up), and the current PE of 26x sits mid-range of its 19-51x 52-week window. The Q2 2026 earnings report in late July represents a near-term catalyst that could confirm or disappoint on the software acceleration narrative. Key risks include the inevitable post-cycle mainframe deceleration, sluggish consulting growth (1% in Q1), elevated debt ($57.7B), and enterprise AI adoption friction flagged in IBM's own research. The balance between solid execution and a stock that has already moved 22% off its April lows warrants a modest positive score.
